Living Well / Free resources

Books, art & creative exploration

A useful way in

Choose one place to begin.

Find something to read, hear, look at, or make, without needing to turn the encounter into an achievement.

Creative work gives attention somewhere to go. You might spend a few minutes with a poem, compare two artworks, listen to a story, or make a simple rhythm. The point is not to complete a cultural checklist; it is to encounter something that holds your interest.

Start with: Project Gutenberg. Find a title or subject and use the browser-reading option to sample a few pages.

Keep the context

Take what is useful, thoughtfully.

Free access and permission to reuse are different. Read the rights information attached to an item before copying it into your own work. Older books may contain dated assumptions or language, and a digital collection represents editorial choices rather than a complete history. Enjoying a work does not require adopting all of its author’s views.

Selections are based on public source review, not a claim that Nolan uses every resource or belongs to the organizations listed.
